Counters start after constant initialization and end after root execution, child joins, cached-value cleanup and the final drain, before runtime shutdown.
limits: Collection disabled, physical freeing enabled. Raw interpretation and ordinary native output are functional references using their usual connection pooling; their transport work differs from this instrumented churn workload. Ownership revision comparisons must use the same connection-closing hooks. Managed allocation/retain counts, charged storage, connection/request finalization and queued-message bytes are measured. Empty I/O task lists establish completed task execution, not reclaimed task-object storage. Stack pools, other raw buffers, allocator/TLS/OS storage, server/process memory and timing are excluded. One native client process makes 1, 16 or 256 batches of remote calls over loopback HTTP/2 to an interpreted greeter. Each response contains integers 1..64. Full batches sum all 64; partial batches sum only the first 32; retained batches sum an initial stream, make and sum a second call while retaining the initial iterator, then reread its first value. Retained batches therefore make twice as many calls. Raw unoptimized interpreter and ordinary native output must agree. Three separate instrumented processes per case count managed allocations/retains/charged bytes, created/finalized connection and stream objects, and requested/freed queued-message bytes including their header and trailing byte. GC is disabled, physical freeing enabled. Counters start after constant initialization. Final counters follow root execution, joining its child tasks and cached-value cleanup, before whole-runtime shutdown. Before the final sample, measurement hooks close every pooled connection and drain all detached I/O tasks. Checkpoints are immediately before each new stream is allocated, after connection selection and request-header preparation; a checkpoint can deliberately include an earlier retained iterator. Excludes other raw buffers, TLS/OS/allocator metadata, server/whole-process memory and timing. Native builds use ordinary -O2. Source, generated C, executables and raw stderr are retained.

Connection-churn variant: measurement-only native hooks close the pool before each new call and after cached-value cleanup, cancel/wait for the detached connection reader and writer, and require zero live I/O tasks and one closed socket per created connection before sampling. Each call uses a new connection. Ordinary native and interpreter executions still use their usual pooling: their output is the functional reference, not an equivalent transport workload. Compare ownership revisions using these same churn hooks; do not use this experiment as a timing comparison with pooled calls. Retained iterators still keep earlier cached values across connection closure. hosts.scope:
One native client process makes 1, 16 or 256 batches of remote calls over loopback HTTP/2 to an interpreted greeter. Each response contains integers 1..64. Full batches sum all 64; partial batches sum only the first 32; retained batches sum an initial stream, make and sum a second call while retaining the initial iterator, then reread its first value. Retained batches therefore make twice as many calls. Raw unoptimized interpreter and ordinary native output must agree. Three separate instrumented processes per case count managed allocations/retains/charged bytes, created/finalized connection and stream objects, and requested/freed queued-message bytes including their header and trailing byte. GC is disabled, physical freeing enabled. Counters start after constant initialization. Final counters follow root execution, joining its child tasks and cached-value cleanup, before whole-runtime shutdown. Before the final sample, measurement hooks close every pooled connection and drain all detached I/O tasks. Checkpoints are immediately before each new stream is allocated, after connection selection and request-header preparation; a checkpoint can deliberately include an earlier retained iterator. Excludes other raw buffers, TLS/OS/allocator metadata, server/whole-process memory and timing. Native builds use ordinary -O2. Source, generated C, executables and raw stderr are retained.

Connection-churn variant: measurement-only native hooks close the pool before each new call and after cached-value cleanup, cancel/wait for the detached connection reader and writer, and require zero live I/O tasks and one closed socket per created connection before sampling. Each call uses a new connection. Ordinary native and interpreter executions still use their usual pooling: their output is the functional reference, not an equivalent transport workload. Compare ownership revisions using these same churn hooks; do not use this experiment as a timing comparison with pooled calls. Retained iterators still keep earlier cached values across connection closure. Drain rows record created/closed connections, live I/O tasks, managed charge, unfinalized connection/request counts and unread message bytes. Scheduler stack pools, other raw buffers and TLS/OS storage remain excluded.
